entries.clue: Rocket Man singer starts to open for Thin White Duke (4,2,5)

annotation.surface: A roll-call of glam-rock personas: Elton John opening the show for David Bowie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thin White Duke' was David Bowie's 1970s persona, and 'Rocket Man singer' pulls you towards pop, but the duke is a medieval one: John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster.
annotation.definitionFit: John of Gaunt, son of Edward III, was Duke of Lancaster.

entries.clue: Sucker embracing a bit of jesting (6)

blocks.note: a jay is a gullible person, a mug
a = per, as in 'five pounds a head'

annotation.walkthrough: The little word 'a' looks like part of 'a bit of jesting', but it is the wordplay: 'a' means per, as in 'twice a day'.
annotation.definitionFit: Japery is jesting or joking, a jape being a practical joke.

entries.clue: Hearts get all aflutter with Andersen fairy tale (6,3,6)

annotation.walkthrough: Andersen looks like the author of the answer, but Hansel and Gretel is from the Brothers Grimm; his name is only letters here.
annotation.definitionFit: Hansel and Gretel is the Grimms' fairy tale of two children and a gingerbread house.

entries.clue: Regarding school education: university life discharged according to plan (2,8)

annotation.surface: A report on school education in which university life gets kicked out.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a policy paper, but every word is an abbreviation or a small chunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Something on schedule happens as planned.

entries.clue: Fine fabric not having uniform look (4)

annotation.surface: A fine cloth without a regular look to it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform look' reads as a single phrase about the fabric, but 'uniform' is only the letter U.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean directing the eyes, the answer implying a long, steady stare.

entries.clue: One from Paris and the German go through subway (9)

entries.clue: In the US, check top of container holding old paper (7)

a lid is the top of a container

annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a verb, but it is the US noun for a restaurant bill; 'top of container' is a whole lid, not a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a newspaper in the small format, usually a popular one.

entries.clue: Maga? It’s … it’s converted millions, it’s an issue for the viewers (11)

annotation.surface: A stammering pundit noting that the MAGA movement has won over millions, and that this matters to television audiences.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'viewers' sound like TV audiences; here they are eyes, and the issue is a sight defect.
annotation.definitionFit: Astigmatism is a defect of the eye that blurs vision, so a problem for those who see.

entries.clue: Plucky male soon embraces old king (9)

indicatorNotes.embraces: to embrace is to put your arms round, so ANON goes round GAME and M

entries.clue: Fish starter of tuna, sashimi-style, left (5)

annotation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered garden weed.

entries.clue: Best man dined out, likely to have forgotten the ring? (6-6)

annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a wedding-day disaster, and the best man is exactly the forgetful figure the answer describes.

indicatorNotes.out from: take ... out from means remove, so T is removed

annotation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone given as medication for diabetes.

entries.clue: Interfere with embedded spy on street (6)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.walkthrough: The hunting picture reads naturally; real meaning royal survives in names like Real Madrid and in the old Spanish coin.

entries.clue: Puzzle session on plush cushions (7)

blocks.note: the letters run from the last letter of session through on and into plush

annotation.walkthrough: 'Cushions' looks like soft furnishing to match plush, but it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to baffle someone so that they do not know what to do.

entries.clue: Giza geezer? Say no about accepting part one (8)

annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a question mark: Giza, home of the pyramids, is in Egypt, and geezer is British slang for a man.

entries.clue: Standard customers for 12 sunloungers? (3,4,3,10)

blocks.note: reads like a travel agent's usual clients; it means the people who typically do this
12 is noon, not a count or a cross-reference: who lounges in the midday sun? Noël Coward's song answers

annotation.surface: A travel agent's profile of the typical buyer of a dozen deckchairs.
annotation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference or a count of loungers, but it is twelve o'clock: the song says only mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun.
annotation.definitionFit: In Noël Coward's song, mad dogs and Englishmen are the only ones who lounge in the noon sun.

entries.clue: Nick long-term prisoner kidnapping retired copper (7)

entries.clue: Actor Moore featured in big budget movie Outbreak (8)

entries.clue: Spooner’s inundation chart that’ll help to deflect dirty water (7)

a map is a chart; its opening M sound is swapped for FL

annotation.surface: A flood-risk map for a scheme to keep filthy water out.
annotation.walkthrough: Say FLOOD MAP with the opening sounds swapped and you get MUD FLAP; both the chart and the flap deal with dirty water, which is why the surface holds together.

entries.clue: Fish Bilk caught in Brooks? (8)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of a word, so NICE drops its last letter

annotation.walkthrough: Satay is skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce, a Malaysian street dish.

entries.clue: My English heart (4)

entries.clue: Remote location not allowed mail (7)

blocks.note: out = not allowed, as in 'that's out'

annotation.surface: A far-flung place where no mail is permitted.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a place post can't reach; the two halves simply join.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small settlement or garrison far from the centre is a remote location.

entries.clue: Ace article in French Times — also, let me see, great leader (9)

blocks.note: er = a hesitation, like 'let me see'

annotation.surface: A hesitant reader praising an excellent piece in a French newspaper about a great leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great leader' is Alexander the Great; the first half reads as a newspaper article in a French Times.
annotation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the Macedonian king who conquered much of the known world.

entries.clue: High-level worker peels jacket off (11)

indicatorNotes.off: off means wrong or spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A worker high up taking off his jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peels jacket off' reads as undressing, but off is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A steeplejack climbs and repairs steeples and chimneys.

entries.clue: Good European soldiers in notorious formation (11)

indicatorNotes.in: G, E and MEN go inside ARRANT

annotation.surface: A good European army in a notorious battle formation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Formation' fits the soldiers, but it is the definition: an arrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: An arrangement is a formation, the way things are set out.
